messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Production p99 latency > 3s for /v1/stream in us-west-2 (prod-inference). Auto-escalation: paging on-call. link: https://grafana.redwood/prod/streams?panelId=12 :rotating_light:

oncall-bot: @alex you were paged by escalation policy 'prod-latency-p99'. Please acknowledge or swap. /oncall ack alex

jen: acked. seeing big tail in streaming p99, p95 also creeping. started investigating.

alex: oncall here — looking. is there a specific node or rack flagged?

sam: infra alerts show GPU node g-42 reporting repeated correctable ECC and thermal throttles since ~10:02 UTC. logs attached.

jen: copying logs snippet:

```
2026-03-15T10:01:07Z g-42 nvidia: GPU 0 correctable ECC error 0x34
2026-03-15T10:01:08Z g-42 nvidia: GPU 0 temperature spike -> 92C throttle
2026-03-15T10:01:09Z g-42 runtime: nvlink reinit
```

lena: we've got streaming stalls correlating with requests hitting that node (kv cache miss rate spike). p99 streaming stalls ~11s at peak, p95 ~1.4s. customer-facing reduction: ~3% of active streams affected, mostly longer sequences.

alex: good. immediate mitigation options: 1) cordon/drain g-42 and evict pods (rollback model placement), 2) route traffic away via routing policy to warm pool, 3) temporarily reduce model size on affected routes (lower context) to avoid long KV sequences. prefer 1 + 2.

jen: agree. initiating drain. /drain-node g-42 --grace=30s (will trigger re-schedule). also bump fallback routing weight to dedicated-warm by 70%.

sam: running cordon: `kubectl cordon node/g-42` -> success. starting drain: `kubectl drain g-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`

jen: evictions in progress. streaming connections will be gracefully migrated where possible; there may be brief retry spikes.

lena: monitoring: p99 dropped from 3.2s -> 1.6s after re-route, stalls reduced from 11s -> 3.5s. still a residual tail.

alex: any sign of hardware failure or is this thermal-only? sam: ECC correctables trending up (20x baseline) then thermal throttle so likely a flaky GPU or cooling issue in that blade. Not seeing permanent ECC uncorrectable yet.

mika: I'll open HW ticket with datacenter ops: blade id rack-r7-b3, g-42. Request on-site fan replacement and run memtest. Ticket: DC-2026-447.

jen: rolling a targeted canary of route fallback for the next 10m to ensure no global regressions. also enabling additional prefix caching to reduce KV churn on remaining nodes.

alex: customer impact note: about 3% sessions affected, primarily chat-streaming with >2k token context. propose status update to SRE-ops and CS to flag top customers that may have seen stalls.

lena: suggested customer message draft: "We're investigating intermittent streaming stalls; mitigations in place. If you're experiencing >10s stalls please contact support with session IDs." thoughts?

jen: fine. sam, please paste list of affected customer IDs (sanitized) to #support-ops. we need to follow up with account owners.

sam: posted redacted list to #support-ops. starting hardware ticket now. GPU vendor also notified.

alex: handoff — I'm going offline in 20m. mika, can you own follow-up (hardware coord + verify remediation)? I'll leave an incident page.

mika: on it. will validate hardware replacement ETA and check p99 in 30m.

jen: ops notes: actions taken: cordon+drain g-42, bumped fallback routing to dedicated-warm pool, enabled extra prefix caching, posted customer alert stub, opened DC ticket DC-2026-447, vendor notified.

lena: metrics update at 10:15 UTC: p99 1.2s, p95 0.9s, stalls <1% sessions. good progress.

alex: thanks team. tagging this as "mitigated" for now; monitor for recurrence. will escalate to Major Incident if uncorrected in 1h.

mika: HW team ETA 3h for on-site swap. will request temporary rack cooling tune.

jen: follow-up postmortem owner: jen (SRE) + infra for hardware. timeline notes: start 10:01 UTC, drain initiated 10:06 UTC, metrics improved 10:10 UTC.

sam: adding root-cause hypothesis: thermal-induced memory correctable error amplification causing GPU driver to throttle; sustained throttle leads to higher latency / stalls due to KV cache pressure. recommend: replace GPU, audit firmware, add cooling thresholds to node-expirer to proactively evacuate at 88C.

alex: agree. also add routing rule to avoid single-node serving for high-token streams (spread across warm pool).

journal-bot: Incident annotated: severity=SEV3, impact=partial streaming stalls, customers_affected=small_percentage, followup=postmortem scheduled.

jen: closing thread here; will open a dedicated postmortem doc with timeline and RCA. ping me or mika for questions. :closed_book:
